subject: Recap & next steps: Aurora HealthTech model-fit check + safeguard request
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex@aurorahealthtech.com>, Rachel Dunn <rachel.d@aurorahealthtech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & next steps: Aurora HealthTech model-fit check + safeguard request

Hi Alex / Rachel—

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Summary of what we heard: Aurora wants a narrow NLU model for triaging inbound clinical intake forms (priority, routing, and extraction). Key constraints: 95%+ precision for high-priority routing, PII redaction, and sub-200ms median latency in your us-west region.

- Redwood recommendation (initial): run two candidate variants in evals: a smaller quantized Llama-2.2B-qlora variant for routing + a tuned 7B instruction-tuned model for extraction. We'll provide benchmark packs and a 1000-sample prompt set (you can see starter prompts in the Drive link below).

- Open risk flagged on the call: Aurora recently noticed a quality delta after a model backend update in another vendor. To avoid surprises, you asked for an emergency safeguard plan if you see regressions during onboarding. Proposed safeguard: pin the serving gateway to a specific model artifact (hash) during the trial and enable a canary policy (5% traffic to new model) for any automatic upgrades; immediate rollback path if diff monitoring shows >3% drop in extraction F1 on your validation set.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll share the eval pack + starter prompt set (attached).
2) Ben | Monica — can you confirm feasibility of: pinning model artifact, creating a canary route, and a fast rollback plan (what we can commit to for a trial environment)?
3) Alex/Rachel — please send a short sample of the 200–300 recent intake forms (PII redacted) and any existing extraction rules so we can seed the evals.

I attached a quick prompt CSV (starter prompts) and a tiny regression snippet example to illustrate the kind of diffs you might see.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-aurora-eval
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/aurora-healthtech

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: aurora_sample_prompts.csv (CSV), regression_snippet_20270228.txt (text)

Thanks for the clear recap. Appreciate the proposed safeguards; those align with what our security/compliance team will want to see. We've attached a small set of redacted intake forms and a short log showing the failure mode we saw previously (you can see fields being misrouted).

Quick questions before we hand off materials:
- When you say "pin model artifact," what granularity is that? Model version number only or full artifact hash?
- What does an emergency rollback look like operationally — how long to reinstate previous artifact?

We'll upload the 300 sample forms to the Drive folder by EOD and included a short PDF with the observed regression examples (filename: aurora-eval-diff-report.pdf).

—Alex

Can you confirm:

- Typical time to rollback to previous artifact (best-case / worst-case) and if we can automate rollback triggered by a monitored regression metric.
- Any constraints on running a 5% canary on production-like traffic for a customer trial.

Ben — can you take first pass on the customer-facing language and proposed commitments? Monica — can infra/ops confirm technical feasibility and estimated rollback latency?

Thanks — Soojin

Soojin —

Short answers for the customer:
- Pinning: We can pin to exact artifact hash in Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we can pin to a specific model build id (we need feature flag enabled for artifact-hash pinning in Hosted—possible for trial if AE signs an exception). We'll propose: "artifact-hash pin for Dedicated/Private; model-build pin for Hosted trial with option to enable artifact pin by request."

- Rollback latency: automated rollback to a previous artifact is typically < 2 minutes for stateless model switches when model is already warmed in the pool; worst-case (cold start + provisioning) ~ 18-25 minutes depending on GPU availability. For trials we can warm a fallback slot to target artifact to guarantee < 3 minutes.

- Canary policy: 5% canary is fine. We can wire a metric monitor that calculates rolling F1 on their validation set (frequency: every 15 minutes). If the rolling F1 drops > 3% relative to baseline for two consecutive windows, we can trigger an automated rollback (requires their OK).

I'll draft a short customer note to set expectations and the exact phrasing. Monica — are those times accurate from infra? Also, what required entitlements do we need on the account to pre-warm fallback artifact?

—Ben
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap & next steps: Aurora HealthTech model-fit check + safeguard request

Ben / Soojin —

Confirmed from infra side. Details to pass to Aurora: 

- Pinning behavior: Hosted trial -> model-build pin (immutable build id). Dedicated/Private -> artifact-hash pin (full artifact hash, inclusive of tokenizer/config). For Hosted, if customer requests artifact-hash pinning we need to enable the "artifactPinning" feature flag on their account (entitlement change, can be done during trial with AE approval).

- Rollback mechanics & SLA: we recommend the following customer commitment: they provide a 300-sample validation set (redacted) that we ingest into their monitoring workspace. We configure a rolling F1 monitor (15m windows). If the monitor trips (>3% F1 drop for 2 windows), the runbook will:
  1) Activate warmed fallback slot (if prewarmed) -> switch traffic to fallback artifact (< 3 minutes).
  2) If fallback not prewarmed -> provision + switch (worst-case 18-25 minutes).
  3) Post-rollback: generate a diff report (token-level and output-level) and push to shared Drive.

- Preconditions for <3min rollback: account must have reserved fallback slot (we charge a small per-hour warming fee during trial) and provide the validation prompt set.

- Canary: 5% canary routing is available. We can configure auto-rollback trigger but recommend manual review for the first two incidents to avoid false positives.

Operational deliverables we can promise for the trial:
- Eval pack + one-click reg tests (we'll upload to Drive).
- Canary routing + rolling monitor configured.
- Optional warmed fallback slot for <3min rollback (fee applies).

I'll prepare a short doc for Aurora that explains the tradeoffs and exact wording. Ben — can you confirm pricing note for the warmed slot and the wording so I can hand to Soojin?

—Monica
Infra Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Next steps & trial commitments (short doc + pricing)

Alex / Rachel—

Thanks for the quick upload. We reviewed the diff PDF and sample forms. Attached are the starter artifacts and a short one-pager describing the safeguard options and expected timelines. Quick bullets for clarity: 

- Pinning: Hosted trial -> model-build pin (we can enable artifact-hash pinning on request). Dedicated/Private -> artifact-hash pin (full).
- Rollback: <3 minutes with warmed fallback (recommended for your SLAs). Otherwise worst-case 20 minutes.
- Canary: 5% by default; auto-rollback threshold proposed at >3% F1 drop over 30 minutes (two 15m windows).
- Cost: warmed fallback slot = $75/hr during trial (covers reserved GPU warm pool). We'll include 8 hours of warm time free for initial onboarding.

Please confirm if Aurora wants us to:
A) Enable pre-warmed fallback slot for trial (we'll provision and reserve)
B) Enable auto-rollback (triggered by monitor) or require manual approval to trigger rollback
C) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive this week with Monica and Aditya to review the eval pack and required validation set formatting

Proposed times for deep-dive: Wed 3/3 09:00-10:00 PT or Thu 3/4 11:00-12:00 PT.

Thanks — we'll draft the short customer doc (I'll attach it here once Ben finalizes the language).

Soojin
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: aurora_sample_prompts.csv, aurora-eval-diff-report.pdf
